toolShell.disclaimerText: The calculations, classifications, and lifestyle suggestions this tool provides are for general wellness and self-assessment reference only, and cannot replace a qualified physician's clinical diagnosis, treatment plan, or prescription advice. If experiencing any physical discomfort or health concern, seek professional help from a licensed medical institution and specialist immediately.

aedTool.bannerTitle: Win the golden 4 minutes! CPR + AED save lives
aedTool.bannerDesc: If someone is unresponsive and not breathing, call for help immediately, dial 119, and get the nearest AED and follow its voice instructions.
aedTool.expandedNotice: No device within 5km — search radius expanded automatically
aedTool.radiusNote: Shows a 5km search radius and exact placement details
aedTool.noResults: No AED locations match these filters. Try a different keyword or clear the "currently open" filter.
aedTool.searchPlaceholder: Search by place name (e.g. HSR station, MRT, school, activity center) or address
aedTool.onlyOpenCheckbox: ⚡ Show only currently open (hide locked/closed sites)
aedTool.mnemonicHeading: 💡 AED first-aid mnemonic: "Call, Call, C, D"
aedTool.step1Detail: Tap both shoulders and call out loudly; check if the chest is rising and falling.
aedTool.step2Detail: Have someone call 119 and quickly bring the nearest AED.
aedTool.step3Detail: Interlace hands and press hard on the lower half of the sternum, 100-120 times per minute, 5-6cm deep.
aedTool.step4Desc: Turn on the AED and follow its voice
aedTool.step4Detail: Attach the pads; everyone steps back while it analyzes the heart rhythm, then press the shock button as instructed.

erStatusTool.dashboardDesc: Auto-synced every 15 minutes from the Ministry of Health and Welfare and each emergency-responsibility hospital | For non-critical conditions, please consider a regular clinic first, to preserve emergency room capacity for critical cases
erStatusTool.searchPlaceholder: Search by hospital name, county/city, or district (e.g. NTUH, Linkou CGMH, Beitou)
erStatusTool.sortNote: Sorted automatically by 119 diversion status and consultation wait count
erStatusTool.loadingBoard: Connecting live to the Ministry of Health and Welfare's nationwide ER board...
erStatusTool.emptyTitle: No emergency-responsibility hospitals match these filters
erStatusTool.emptyHint: Try clearing the keyword or switching the region filter
erStatusTool.fullReportedBanner: 🚨 119 full-capacity notice: ER capacity is saturated — please avoid unless it's a major emergency!
erStatusTool.tip1Text: Historical ER data shows 7pm-11pm nightly is the busiest period, with average wait times increasing by 40% or more.
erStatusTool.tip2Text: Emergency rooms triage patients (Level 1 resuscitation, Level 2 critical, Level 3 urgent, Level 4 less urgent, Level 5 non-urgent) — non-critical patients should expect to wait while critical cases are treated first.
erStatusTool.tip3Text: For a mild fever, minor stomach upset, or a scrape, a daytime visit to a local clinic saves significant wait time and reduces the emergency-room copayment.
